title: RNA and Transcription
text: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is a polymeric molecule essential in various biological roles including coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes. Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes for protein synthesis. Transfer RNA (tRNA) brings amino acids to ribosomes during translation. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) forms the structural and catalytic components of ribosomes. Non-coding RNAs such as microRNAs (miRNAs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) play regulatory roles. The discovery of RNA's catalytic properties, as ribozymes, challenged the view that enzymes must be proteins and suggested RNA may have played a central role in the origin of life.
